clue.text: Soft gold characteristic of this form of art

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
or is the heraldic word for gold
a characteristic is a trait, a distinguishing quality

explanation.surface: Soft golden tones are the hallmark of this kind of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of this' is a link: the pieces themselves are said to belong to the art form being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted likeness of a person is a recognised genre of art.

clue.text: Nothing memorable in the last act on the world stage

definitions.text: Nothing memorable in the last act on the world stage

parts.words: Nothing memorable in the last act on the world stage
parts.note: echoes Jaques's seven ages of man speech, whose last scene is mere forgetfulness

explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It, 'All the world's a stage' ends with 'second childishness and mere' forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Total forgetfulness, a state where nothing is remembered.

clue.text: Put binding on a wind instrument as a means of sound reproduction

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is put on top of the second

parts.note: tape is a strip used for binding
the recorder is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: Someone wraps tape round a flute-like instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that records and plays back sound on magnetic tape.

clue.text: A protoplasmal primordial atomic globule was Pooh-Bah's

definitions.text: A protoplasmal primordial atomic globule was Pooh-Bah's

parts.words: A protoplasmal primordial atomic globule was Pooh-Bah's
parts.note: Pooh-Bah in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado boasts of tracing his family back to a primordial globule

explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado, Pooh-Bah says he can trace his ancestry back to a protoplasmal primordial atomic globule.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Storm split a party

parts.note: torn means ripped or split
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political party breaks apart in a storm of dissent.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Pulse fast, over one-fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the rest

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A racing heartbeat goes over one hundred and fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, such as this small lens-shaped one.

clue.text: Jacobson's live broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered about, so the letters of live are shuffled

explanation.surface: A man called Jacobson is broadcasting live.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Jacobson's' as 'Jacob's son is': the definition is one of the twelve sons of Jacob in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this son of Jacob founded the priestly tribe.

clue.text: A bit of a break

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to shatter into pieces

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a small piece; as a verb, to shatter into pieces.

clue.text: Superintendent who keeps an eye on deliveries

definitions.meaning: a person in charge who supervises workers

definitions.text: who keeps an eye on deliveries
definitions.meaning: someone watching the overs, sets of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six deliveries (balls bowled), so a watcher of overs keeps an eye on deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor watches over others' work; whimsically, a spectator of cricket overs.

clue.text: Agitation, should this flying control fail?

definitions.meaning: a state of nervous excitement or panic
a hinged surface on an aircraft wing used to control lift

explanation.surface: A pilot would certainly panic if a wing control surface failed in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should this ... fail?' links the two senses: failure of the wing part would cause the panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A panic or fluster is one sense; a hinged wing surface on an aircraft is the other.

clue.text: A symbolically unending circle of stones

definitions.text: A symbolically unending circle of stones

parts.words: A symbolically unending circle of stones
parts.note: a band set all round with gems, given to represent love that lasts forever; 'circle of stones' tempts one toward a megalithic monument

explanation.definitionFit: This band of jewels symbolises everlasting love, often given on an anniversary.

clue.text: Retract most of article put up in this, being obstinate

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the word for retract

parts.note: to recant is to retract a statement

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the letters are written upwards, read in reverse
most of means the word article loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Taking back much of a piece published here would be stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims ARTICLE to ARTICL; 'put up' turns it to LCITRA; 'in' places that inside RECANT after RECA. 'this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubbornly defiant person resists authority.

clue.text: Like the speech that isn't reported

definitions.text: Like the speech that isn't reported

parts.words: Like the speech that isn't reported
parts.note: grammar distinguishes quoting someone's exact words from reported (...) speech

explanation.definitionFit: Quoting someone's actual words is the grammatical opposite of reported speech.

clue.text: Being frail in health makes Ted and Alice worried

indicators.note: worried in the sense of pulled about, so the names Ted and Alice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple fret over someone's poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link; the eight letters of TED and ALICE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sickly or easily ill is said to be in fragile health.

clue.text: Winding road ran here in the Pyrenees

indicators.note: a winding route twists about, so the letters of road and ran are mixed

explanation.surface: A twisting mountain road runs through this region of the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny principality lies between France and Spain in those mountains.

clue.text: A month in England, a year in Paris, an age in Rome

parts.note: August is the eighth month of the English calendar
an is French for year

explanation.surface: A traveller's itinerary: a month in England, a year in France, an era in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Augustan age was the reign of the emperor Augustus, a golden era of Latin literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the reign of Augustus, the classical golden era of Roman literature.

clue.text: Face shock treatment in a manner of speaking

parts.note: the face of a clock or watch is its dial
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A face given electric shock therapy, in a figurative way of putting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional variety of a language is a particular way of talking.

clue.text: I clear about ten through being inexperienced

indicators.note: about means the word for clear goes round the other pieces

parts.note: net means clear, as in clear profit after deductions
X is the Roman numeral for ten
per means through, by means of

explanation.surface: Someone explains clearing up about ten through lack of experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking skill or practice, unskilled.

clue.text: Such as the interest shown in this enclosure?

definitions.meaning: interest calculated on interest already earned, a banking term

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the interest is on display inside a fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest added to accumulated interest has that name; a walled area of buildings is another sense.

clue.text: Subject for Raphael — the same again in "Food from Heaven"

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: manna is the food sent from heaven to the Israelites
do, short for ditto, means the same again

explanation.surface: An art historian notes the same theme repeated in a painting titled Food from Heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Raphael painted many images of the Virgin Mary, so she is his subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin Mary was a favourite subject of the Renaissance painter Raphael.

clue.text: Flower of the forest one found in Georgia

indicators.note: found in says these pieces sit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
the Forest of Arden, the English woodland of As You Like It
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bloom from the woods turns up in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden is a historic forest in Warwickshire, England, the setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant white-blossomed shrub of the madder family.

clue.text: Explain it without showing one to be a fool

indicators.note: showing means the letters are on view inside the words explain it without

explanation.surface: Explain it without letting someone look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one to be' is a link; 'Explain' tempts as a definition but just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Noted variations of this wartime coding machine

definitions.meaning: Elgar's orchestral work of musical portraits, the Variations on an Original Theme
the German cipher device of World War II broken at Bletchley Park

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes: Elgar composed the famous Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Variations carry this title, and so did the German cipher device.

clue.text: Brownshirt's odd reports about motor accident

indicators.note: about means the first set of letters goes round the second
odd signals that reports is to be rearranged
a motor accident leaves things mangled, so motor's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Strange reports emerge about a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' makes STORPER from REPORTS; 'accident' makes MTROO from MOTOR; 'about' puts MTROO inside STOR...PER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi SA paramilitaries wore brown shirts and were called assault troops.

clue.text: Betting on starters for the Old Donkey Derby Stakes

indicators.note: starters means the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Placing bets at a donkey race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the betting prices offered against a result.

clue.text: Lords and ladies a strange, if wild, combination

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Aristocrats of both sexes make an odd mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Lords and ladies is the British country name of the wild cuckoo-pint plant; 'if wild, combination' is surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords-and-ladies is a folk name for the cuckoo-pint, a wild plant of that genus.

clue.text: Test for part of accountant's work one takes on

parts.note: an audit is the inspection of accounts by an accountant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An accountant's job includes a test that the books are right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link; the pieces stand in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors try out for a role in a performance trial.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon pose struck by Haigha

parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass the messenger Haigha keeps adopting odd postures, explained as Anglo-Saxon

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's Alice says the messenger wriggles; the King explains Haigha is an Anglo-Saxon messenger with Anglo-Saxon poses of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pose or bodily stance is the old sense of the word.
